<action type="say">
Under this login, I can only see your two loans, so that personal checking is almost certainly linked to a different customer profile or hidden in the app.

Here are the most common ways to surface it so you can see the balance:

1. Check for another login/profile  
   - If you’ve ever:  
     - Opened the checking at a branch earlier than the loans, or  
     - Changed usernames/emails over the years,  
     that checking might sit under an older username.  
   - Try:  
     - “Forgot username” on the bank’s sign‑in page (using your SSN and card/account info), or  
     - Any other username/email you might have used.

2. Look for “hidden” or “closed” accounts in the app/website  
   In many banking apps/websites there’s a section like:  
   - “Accounts” → “Manage accounts” / “Show hidden accounts” / “Display preferences”  
   - If you see your checking there, enable “Show in overview” or similar, then go back to the main accounts screen to see the balance.

3. Check for “Link existing account” (same-bank)  
   - Some banks split relationships into separate “profiles” and let you link them:  
   - Look for: “Link an existing [Bank Name] account” / “Combine profiles” in Settings or Profile.  
   - You’ll usually need:  
     - The checking account number and routing number, or  
     - A debit card number tied to that checking.

4. If none of that works  
   - Call the bank or use secure chat and say:  
     “My personal checking account isn’t visible in online banking, but my loans are. Can you check if my checking is on a different profile and link it to this one?”  
   - They can move or link the checking so it appears next to your loans, then you’ll see the balance immediately.

If you tell me:
- Whether you’re on the mobile app or website  
- The approximate year you opened that checking  

I can give very specific, click‑by‑click instructions for what to try next.</action>

<action type="say">
Got it—mobile app, personal checking from around 2015. I’ll walk you through what usually works in this situation.

1) First, look for hidden or filtered accounts  
In the mobile app, try this path (names vary slightly by bank, but the ideas are similar):

- Open the app and sign in.
- Go to the main “Accounts” or “Home” screen.
- Look for:
  - A filter icon, “Show/Hide accounts,” or
  - A gear/settings icon on the accounts list, or
  - A menu item like “Manage accounts,” “Account display,” or “Customize accounts.”
- In that screen:
  - Check for sections like “Hidden accounts,” “Inactive accounts,” or “Do not show.”
  - If you see your checking listed there, toggle it ON or select “Show in overview.”
- Go back to the main accounts screen and see if the checking now appears with a balance.

2) If it’s not hidden: try “Link / Add existing account” (same bank)  
Still in the app:

- Tap the main menu (often ≡, “More,” or a profile icon).
- Look for one of these:
  - “Link accounts”
  - “Add existing [Bank Name] accounts”
  - “Combine profiles” / “Merge relationships”
  - “Profile & Settings” → “Accounts” / “Linked accounts”
- If you find something like “Add existing account”:
  - Choose “I already have an account with [Bank Name].”
  - It may ask for:
    - Your checking account number (from a check / old statement), or
    - A debit card number linked to that checking, plus last 4 of SSN, DOB, etc.
  - Follow the prompts to link it; after that, the checking should appear on the accounts screen with the balance.

3) If you still don’t see it: contact support with exact wording  
Because your checking is older (2015), it’s common for it to sit on an older “customer profile” not tied to this login. In the app:

- Open “Support,” “Help & Support,” or “Messages/Secure chat,” or call the number in the app.
- Tell them something close to this:
  - “My personal checking account opened around 2015 isn’t showing in my mobile banking. Under this login I only see my loans. Can you check whether my checking is on a different online profile or customer ID, and link it so it appears under this login?”
- Have ready (if you can):
  - Checking account number or old check,
  - Last 4 of SSN,
  - Approx. date opened (2015),
  - Mailing address on the account.

They can then join the profiles or add that checking to this login. Once they do, just refresh the app and you’ll see the checking with its balance.

If you tell me your bank’s name (e.g., Chase, Wells Fargo, etc.), I can try to map these steps more exactly to the labels/buttons you’ll see in that specific app.</action>
